questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.question:
Consider the following code written in a pass-by-reference language like FORTRAN and these statements about the code. 

subroutine swap(ix,iy) 
     it = ix 
L1 : ix = iy 
L2 : iy = it 
    end 
    ia = 3 
    ib = 8 
    call swap (ia, ib+5)
    print *, ia, ib 
    end

S1: The compiler will generate code to allocate a temporary nameless cell, initialize it to 13, and pass the address of the cell to swap 
S2: On execution the code will generate a runtime error on line L1 
S3: On execution the code will generate a runtime error on line L2 
S4: The program will print 13 and 8 
S5: The program will print 13 and -2

questions.title: GATE EE 2017 | GA Question: 9
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.question:
The following C function takes a single-linked list of integers as a parameter and rearranges the elements of the list. The function is called with the list containing the integers $1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7$ in the given order. What will be the contents of the list after function completes execution?

struct node {
    int value;
    struct node *next;
};

void rearrange(struct node *list) {
    struct node *p, *q;
    int temp;
    if (!list || !list -> next) return;
    p = list; q = list -> next;
    while(q) {
        temp = p -> value; p->value =  q -> value;
        q->value = temp; p = q ->next;
        q = p? p ->next : 0;
    }   
}

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.question: Which of the following statements about synchronous and asynchronous I/O is NOT true?
questions.rawQuestionHtml:
Which of the following statements about synchronous and asynchronous I/O is NOT true?

  1. An ISR is invoked on completion of I/O in synchronous I/O but not in asynchronous I/O

  2. In both synchronous and asynchronous I/O, an ISR (Interrupt Service Routine) is invoked after completion of the I/O

  3. A process making a synchronous I/O call waits until I/O is complete, but a process making an asynchronous I/O call does not wait for completion of the I/O

  4. In the case of synchronous I/O, the process waiting for the completion of I/O is woken up by the ISR that is invoked after the completion of I/O
